title: [Perf] Tune GLM-5.3-Flash block-FP8 MoE for H20
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Add the H20 block-FP8 Triton MoE configuration for GLM-5.3-Flash at TP4 (288 experts, per-rank MoE intermediate width 512, 128×128 weight blocks), and read its nested text configuration in `benchmark_moe.py`.

The code under review is `eb34e115d041ac685fa38eadf8eae6c51d61dc23`, based on main `39e6a1aa`. The diff keeps 195 lines of generated configuration data, 9 parsing lines, 45 regression-test lines and one CI dependency line. The 35-line tuning guide was moved out of the code diff into this description. The requested ideal total of fewer than 100 added lines is not met; retaining all generated token-count entries preserves nearest-entry selection boundaries.

## Current-source H20 validation (2026-10-28)

The tuned run has six fewer correct GSM8K answers: strict-match **1225/1319 → 1219/1319**, flexible-extract **1226/1319 → 1220/1319** (both −0.454890 percentage points). AIME25 changes from **19/30 → 21/30**. These are one temperature-0 run per arm; quality equivalence is not established.

Each GSM8K filter has 50 discordant questions: 28 correct only in baseline and 22 correct only in tuned. Their union across filters contains 51 questions. [Per-question official labels, reference answers and original responses](https://github.com/mengziheng/vllm/blob/cce97b1ad98a315f7abffebe1c87d758d109051c/reports/pair2-gsm8k-discordance.json) are retained without rescoring.

All 28 workloads completed with command exit 0. Each of the 24 serving runs has 128 successful measured requests and 16 successful warmups. Actual benchmark inputs match across arms, and all four complete logged test-document sets match the pinned official test-split digests. Both model servers and the launcher exited cleanly; the pool reported no foreign GPU process contamination.

Three-run median **total token throughput (input + output tokens/s)**, baseline → tuned; ranges show the three observed run values, not confidence intervals:
- 8192/1: **6791.86 → 6755.25 tokens/s (-0.54%)**; baseline range 6784.61–6820.02, tuned 6704.06–6766.72.
- 2048/512: **3567.37 → 4097.71 tokens/s (+14.87%)**; baseline range 3552.19–3588.29, tuned 3971.54–4320.93.
- 512/1024: **1908.55 → 2302.18 tokens/s (+20.62%)**; baseline range 1820.47–1911.85, tuned 2189.84–2311.67.
- 512/128: **3992.04 → 4683.60 tokens/s (+17.32%)**; baseline range 3931.88–3999.38, tuned 4590.94–4800.80.

The prefill-heavy 8192/1 case does not improve in this pair. The three other cases show higher median throughput. These results apply to this fixed H20 TP4 block-FP8/MTP3 protocol; they do not establish a universal speedup or accuracy equivalence.

Evidence: [all 24 original benchmark CLI outputs](https://github.com/mengziheng/vllm/blob/cce97b1ad98a315f7abffebe1c87d758d109051c/reports/official-bench-stdout-all.txt), [all four original accuracy CLI outputs](https://github.com/mengziheng/vllm/blob/cce97b1ad98a315f7abffebe1c87d758d109051c/reports/official-accuracy-stdout-all.txt), [machine-readable per-run values and medians](https://github.com/mengziheng/vllm/blob/cce97b1ad98a315f7abffebe1c87d758d109051c/reports/pair2-summary.json), [actual logged documents vs official dataset digests](https://github.com/mengziheng/vllm/blob/cce97b1ad98a315f7abffebe1c87d758d109051c/reports/pair2-logged-doc-audit.json), [complete raw commands, environments, results, responses, source/native proofs and clean-exit receipts](https://github.com/mengziheng/vllm/blob/cce97b1ad98a315f7abffebe1c87d758d109051c/raw/fullpair-v10-pair2-48781766/), [native build receipts and loader checks](https://github.com/mengziheng/vllm/blob/cce97b1ad98a315f7abffebe1c87d758d109051c/native/), and [archived historical PR description](https://github.com/mengziheng/vllm/blob/cce97b1ad98a315f7abffebe1c87d758d109051c/reports/PR-description-before-native-validation.md).

## Runtime repair and provenance

The comparison uses two checkouts of the same PR commit and the same freshly built native libraries. The baseline removes only the target H20 MoE JSON; the tuned checkout retains it. Both run sequentially on the same four H20 GPUs, with the same model files, client, dataset revisions, seeds, resource limits and server arguments.

The original startup failure came from current Python wrappers calling older native libraries: FlashMLA passed 14 arguments to a 13-argument extension; MLA cache writes passed 7 to a 6-argument extension. The required ten native targets were rebuilt from the current source and pinned dependencies, including FlashMLA, the core/cache and MoE libraries, FlashKDA, DeepGEMM and FA3. Fresh-process loader checks confirmed the assembled module paths and current schemas. The model runner verifies the frozen files and selected backend. Separate read-only snapshots record the target native libraries mapped by the actual server and worker processes. Build commands, source revisions, CMake cache, compile commands, stdout/stderr, generated-file receipts and loader output are included with the raw evidence.

This is a build of the required execution paths on the fixed CUDA 13 / Torch 2.13 environment. It is not a clean build of every main-branch target. The main CMake Torch 2.14 expectation and FA recipe Torch 2.4 warning remain in the logs. Source identity comes from the actual Git commit and native receipts; installed distribution metadata from the common environment is recorded separately.

### Evaluation protocol

The executable scripts and full command/environment/exit receipts are linked with the results. Every accuracy request retains its response, input and reference. The two arms must pass source/native provenance checks, model readiness plus a real request, complete sample/request counts, and equality of actual accuracy inputs and benchmark prompts before a paired summary is produced.

- GSM8K: all 1,319 test samples, 5-shot, `local-completions`, 256 generated-token limit; report the official strict-match and flexible-extract scores and standard errors.
- AIME25: all 30 test samples, 0-shot, `local-chat-completions` with the model chat template, 32,768 generated-token limit. This is one temperature-0 attempt per question, not a multi-attempt estimate.
- Accuracy uses lm-evaluation-harness 0.4.13, temperature 0, concurrency 8, seed 20261028 and no request retries. GSM8K and AIME25 dataset revisions are fixed in the linked offline-cache preparation receipt and reused by both arms.
- `vllm bench serve`: input/output lengths 8192/1, 2048/512, 512/1024 and 512/128; three runs per shape and arm, each with 16 warm-up and 128 measured requests. Temperature 0, ignored EOS, unlimited request rate, maximum client concurrency 128, per-run seed and cache salt fixed across arms. Every warm-up and measured request must succeed. Actual prompt digests are matched across arms.
- Both servers use TP4, Triton MoE, maximum model length 40000, 32 sequences, 4096 batched tokens, GPU memory utilization 0.92 and MTP with 3 speculative tokens. All model weights are reused read-only; all caches, temporary files and raw output are on the independent data disk.

Both arms keep `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=0`; the fixed seeds and temperature-0 settings do not establish bitwise batch invariance. The 62-shard local checkpoint is identified by the existing structural/header receipt and read-only start/end file-stat checks; tensor bodies were not rehashed. Server startup and the 16 warm-up requests are outside the official timed region; work occurring during measurement remains included. Three-run medians describe this workload and fixed environment. They are not confidence intervals or an across-workload speedup. Per-run values and official CLI output remain available; latency percentiles from separate runs are not pooled.

### Regression tests

The real Transformers GLM config cases check that the benchmark uses the MoE width (2048) instead of the dense MLP width (12288), and reads outer FP8 block metadata. The CPU tests passed 3/3; removing only the 9-line GLM branch produced the expected 2 failures and 1 pass, then restoring it passed 3/3. CUDA stayed uninitialized. Applicable pre-commit checks passed, including CI test selection, Ruff, formatting, mypy and SPDX. These unchanged results are reused; the new native/GPU checks cover the runtime paths they did not exercise.

Results apply to the listed H20 TP4 block-FP8 workloads. Historical tuning and v0.30 / CUDA 12.9 measurements remain in the archived prior description.

<details>
<summary>Triton MoE configuration usage and retuning</summary>

When GLM-5.3-Flash uses the Triton fused MoE backend on NVIDIA H20 at TP4,
vLLM automatically loads the bundled configuration for 288 experts, a per-rank
intermediate size of 512, and FP8 weights with 128×128 quantization blocks.
No additional flag is needed for this configuration. It tunes the existing
Triton backend; it does not change which MoE backend vLLM selects.
Batch-invariant execution (`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`) uses its fixed configuration
instead of tuned configurations.

To search the benchmark's parameter space for this model from a source checkout:

```bash
python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe.py \
  --model /path/to/GLM-5.3-Flash --tp-size 4 --dtype fp8_w8a8 \
  --tune --save-dir ./moe-tuned
```

The benchmark reads the model configuration and uses synthetic inputs; it does
not load the model weights. Its batch size is the number of tokens passed to
MoE, rather than the number of serving requests. Use `--batch-size` to select
the token counts to tune. Set `VLLM_TUNED_CONFIG_FOLDER` to the generated
configuration directory to evaluate the results in vLLM. Validate numerical
correctness and model behavior before adopting new settings, and measure
performance with the intended hardware, software versions, and serving workload.

For example, start a new server process with the generated configuration and
explicitly select Triton:

```bash
VLLM_TUNED_CONFIG_FOLDER=/absolute/path/to/moe-tuned \
  vllm serve /path/to/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --moe-backend triton
```

</details>
